comment: Where each fact about this chip stands, given that no document names the part.

sources.document: None for the OBC1. Nintendo's OAM structure is documented and is what this chip feeds.
sources.reference: snes9x, pinned by commit in conformance/pinned.json.
sources.cartridge: The one cartridge that carries this chip, whose driver is the only program that ever drove it. Read out of its own code by snes-driver-python, in both the American and the European release, and recorded in conformance/cartridges.json.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. No manufacturer document for the OBC1 is known to exist.
divergences.referenceDoes: Gives every register address, both base addresses and the memory size.
divergences.reasoning: One cartridge carried this chip, so there is no corpus of independent drivers to cross-check against and no second implementation that was not written by reading the same one. Everything except the packed offset rests on that. Since 2026-08-25 the register addresses no longer rest on that alone. conformance/against_cartridges.py walks the driver routine in both releases of the one cartridge without running any of it, and six of the seven addresses this package treats as registers are addresses that code reaches: 0x7FF0 through 0x7FF3, 0x7FF5 and 0x7FF6. The American and European builds agree on every one the American build reaches. That is the cartridge saying where the registers are rather than an emulator saying it, and it does not extend to what any of them does. The seventh, 0x7FF4, is reached as well: the stores to 0x7FF3 that reach it are two bytes wide, which the walk does not establish and so counts as one. A headless MAME 0.289 run of each release for 3,600 frames saw 0x7FF4 written from six instructions in bank 0x82, and the cartridge bytes at each, an ora #$0200 or and #$FDFF with a two-byte immediate followed by a store to 0x7FF3, confirm the width without the emulator. Since 2026-10-19 the recorded reading reaches 0x7FF4 too: every access the walk makes carries a width label, known, executed, traced or assumed, and the stores to 0x7FF3 take their width from snes-driver-python's MAME trace, labelled traced. Of 708 accesses across both releases, 21 are known, 34 traced and 653 assumed and replayed as one byte.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A die photograph, a board schematic, or a Nintendo application note naming the part.

divergences.documentSays: Nintendo documents OAM as 128 sprites of four bytes each, followed by two bits per sprite.
divergences.referenceDoes: Uses 0x200 as the offset from a base to the packed attributes.
divergences.reasoning: 128 times 4 is 512, which is 0x200. This chip lays its memory out the way OAM is laid out, because feeding OAM is the whole of what it does, so Nintendo's figure is evidence about this chip even though Nintendo never described this chip. It is the one constant here that does not rest on a reimplementation.
divergences.wouldReopenIt: Finding that the offset is not the OAM low table size, which would mean the layouts do not mirror each other after all.

divergences.referenceDoes: Behaves as the one driver that exists needs it to.
divergences.reasoning: Sibling packages cross-check a behaviour across dozens of cartridges, and one driver could be wrong where thirty six could not be wrong the same way. Here there is one driver, so anything it never exercises is unconstrained: the chip could do something else entirely with a base address that cartridge never selects and nothing would notice.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A second cartridge carrying this chip, which does not exist, or a die photograph.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. The width of an access is set by whoever called the routine making it.
divergences.referenceDoes: Nothing comparable: a reimplementation answers whatever access the console makes.
divergences.reasoning: conformance/against_cartridges.py labels every access width known, executed, traced or assumed, and replays an assumed one as one byte, which can miss the second byte of a word. Measured on 2026-10-19 against snes-driver-python at adc1b8c: 708 accesses across both releases, 21 known, 0 executed, 34 traced, 653 assumed; walks from 292 and 291 sites rest on an assumed width and are named under assumedAt in conformance/cartridges.json. Every register is reached by an access that is not assumed; 0x7FFD and 0x7FFF only through assumed ones.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A trace reaching each site under assumedAt, or a decode the walker can follow: a sweep from the vectors arriving at the routine with its width.

divergences.referenceDoes: Answers immediately, as this model does.
divergences.reasoning: How long the chip takes to answer is unmodelled and unmeasured.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A measurement on a real cartridge.
